statement: Reconciling a receipted constitutional state against a fresh external read never rewrites that state: agreement records the check, and disagreement produces a NEW, independently-receipted discrepancy event — the state field itself is only ever changed by a subsequent verified-and-receipted transition, never by a reconciliation read.
classification: Operator directive, 2026-08-08, verbatim: "Reconciliation does not rewrite constitutional history. It produces new evidence... If it does not [agree], that discrepancy itself becomes a new event requiring treatment — not an excuse to silently rewrite history."

canaries.assertion: reconcilePulseConstitutionalState against a later disagreeing partner read writes horizen_reconciliation_discrepancy_recorded naming the disagreeing fields and leaves partner_authorization_requests.state at CONFIRMED — the acceptance-invariant assertion itself. On agreement, writes no discrepancy receipt and touches no state field.

occurrences.defect: Before this change, the only reread function (verifyHorizenTransparencyActivation) that could run against a settled row was scoped to non-CONFIRMED states specifically so a reread could never overwrite CONFIRMED — but that was a structural accident of which states were reachable, not a named rule, and nothing existed to reconcile an ALREADY-CONFIRMED row at all, so the 'never rewrite' property had no enforcement point of its own once such a capability was added.

notes: A genuine subsequent state change (revocation, expiry) is EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE for the reconciliation function itself — it requires a new, separately verified and receipted transition, issued as its own deliberate act. Automating that from a disagreement is the exact shortcut this invariant forbids.

reconcilePulseConstitutionalState is not wired into any automatic cadence yet (no click, no poll, no cron) — see the parent resolution record's rejectedApproaches. The 'never rewrites' property is enforced regardless of how/when reconciliation is triggered, but 'periodic' reconciliation in the operator's literal sense (time-scheduled) remains a follow-up decision, not yet built.
